application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A TypeScript HTTP client built on the Fetch API, with configurable requests, response parsing, retries, hooks, and normalized errors.
application.purpose: Make Fetch API requests more convenient and type-safe across applications and runtimes that provide a compatible fetch implementation.

domains.name: HTTP client and request configuration
domains.description: Creates configured fetch clients and prepares request options, headers, bodies, and timeouts.

domains.name: URL and query construction
domains.description: Combines base URLs with paths and adds or updates query parameters.

domains.name: Response parsing and lifecycle
domains.description: Selects response parsing behavior, runs request and response hooks, and handles HTTP failures and retries.

domains.name: Fetch errors
domains.description: Builds errors containing request, response, status, and parsed response data context.

domains.name: Typed fetch API
domains.description: Defines TypeScript request options and maps response types for callers.

terminology.meaning: The main convenience function: makes a request and returns its parsed data. Its raw method returns the response object.
Request configuration such as method, headers, body, base URL, query parameters, timeout, retry policy, and hooks.
Callbacks invoked at request, request-error, response, and response-error stages.
The requested or inferred format for response data, such as JSON, text, blob, array buffer, or stream.
A normalized error that exposes the request context and, when available, response data and status information.
HTTP status codes eligible for retry when retries are enabled; callers can provide a custom list.

Joins a base URL and path while avoiding duplicate or missing separators.
Adds a configured base path to a request URL when it is not already present.
Removes a trailing slash from a URL path, with special handling for the root path.
Adds or updates URL query parameters, omitting undefined values.
Converts query values into strings suitable for URL parameters.
Creates a contextual fetch error with request details and available response data and status.
Identifies HTTP methods treated as payload methods, including POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE.
Determines whether a request body can be serialized as JSON rather than passed through as a non-JSON payload.
Chooses a default response parser based on the response Content-Type.
Combines per-request and default options, including query parameters and headers.
Combines default and request headers, allowing request headers to override matching defaults.
Runs one or more lifecycle hooks in sequence and awaits their completion.
Creates a fetch client that prepares requests, invokes hooks, parses responses, and handles HTTP errors and retries.
Decides whether a failed request should be retried and otherwise throws a normalized fetch error.

Example program that requests a URL returning an HTTP error status and logs the result or failure.

applicationFacts: The default exported ofetch and $fetch clients are created using globalThis.fetch when available.
The client supports creating additional clients with default options and optional custom fetch implementations.
Requests can specify a base URL, query parameters, headers, body, timeout, retry settings, and lifecycle hooks.
JSON-serializable bodies for payload methods are serialized automatically, with JSON headers added when appropriate.
Response parsing can be selected explicitly or inferred from Content-Type; JSON parsing uses destr by default.
HTTP response errors from status codes 400 through 599 are thrown unless ignoreResponseError is enabled.
The source defines default retry status codes of 408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504.
The API exposes typed response options, including JSON, text, blob, array buffer, and stream.
